title: Infection Spread Simulation
prompt:
Implement a five-part synchronous infection simulation. Use integer cell states: `HEALTHY = 0`, `INFECTED = 1`, `IMMUNE = 2`, `DEAD = 3`, and `BURNED = 4`. All daily transitions must read the same start-of-day grid, and no function may mutate its input. The default neighborhood is four-directional.

### Part 1 — Basic propagation

Implement `simulate_basic(grid, infection_threshold=1, directions=DIR4)`. A healthy plant becomes infected when it has at least `infection_threshold` infected neighbors. Infection is permanent. Return `(days_to_stability, final_grid)`.

### Part 2 — Static immunity

Implement `simulate_with_immunity(...)`. Immune plants never become infected and never transmit. Other rules match Part 1.

### Part 3 — Recovery and immunity

Implement `simulate_recovery(grid, infectious_days, infection_threshold=1, directions=DIR4)`. An infected plant transmits for exactly `infectious_days` daily updates, then becomes immune. A newly infected plant begins transmitting on the next day's snapshot and receives the full timer. Return `(days_to_stability, final_grid)`.

### Part 4 — Pending death

Implement `simulate_pending_death(grid, infectious_days, death_threshold, infection_threshold=1, directions=DIR4)`. If an infected plant has at least `death_threshold` infected neighbors on any sick day, permanently mark it doomed. Infection day counts for a newly infected plant. On its normal recovery day, a doomed plant becomes dead; otherwise it becomes immune. Return `(days_to_stability, dead_count, final_grid)`.

### Part 5 — Optimal initial burn

Implement `best_initial_burn(grid, infectious_days, death_threshold, infection_threshold=1, directions=DIR4)`. Before the first simulated day, burn exactly one complete row or column. Evaluate every action with Part 4 and minimize `(dead_count, stable_days)`. Break remaining ties by rows before columns, then lower index. Return `(dead_count, stable_days, axis, index, final_grid)`.

example.reasoning: The infection advances one cell per synchronous day.
